metadata.topic: I’ll develop an evidence-grounded literature foundation for an IEEE paper on **NeuroChain**, a causal neural-DSP vocal processor for speech and singing that targets sub-10 ms end-to-end latency while preserving formants, vowel identity, timbre, and performer identity. The research will retrieve and compare at least 40 relevant sources spanning formant analysis and tracking, real-time enhancement, vocoders/DDSP, learned audio effects, singing-voice processing, efficient inference, evaluation methods, and dataset licensing. It will distinguish sourced facts, cross-paper interpretations, and unvalidated hypotheses; report unsupported quantitative fields as “not reported”; and analyze latency definitions rather than treating algorithmic, buffering, inference, and system latency as interchangeable. The report will evaluate the proposed closed-form formant-safety projection against the closest retrieved work, develop and rank 5–8 feasible contributions, and conclude with one recommended three-month paper direction, validation plan, IEEE-style outline, comparison tables, and fully traceable references.

sub_topics.title: Evidence Corpus and Reporting Framework
sub_topics.overview: Define the search, screening, classification, and citation-tracing process for at least 40 relevant sources. Establish rules for separating sourced facts, cross-paper interpretations, and unvalidated hypotheses, while marking unavailable quantitative details as "not reported."

sub_topics.title: Formant, Vowel, Timbre, and Performer-Identity Preservation
sub_topics.overview: Review speech and singing acoustics, formant estimation and tracking, source-filter interactions, pitch-dependent challenges, and perceptual factors governing vowel, timbre, and identity preservation. Identify measurable safety constraints and limitations of existing tracking methods.

sub_topics.title: Neural-DSP Vocal Processing Landscape
sub_topics.overview: Compare causal speech enhancement, neural vocoders, differentiable DSP, learned audio effects, and singing-voice processing systems by architecture, controllability, audio quality, conditioning, and preservation behavior. Organize the closest prior work into traceable comparison tables without conflating distinct task settings.

sub_topics.title: Real-Time Architecture, Efficient Inference, and Latency Accounting
sub_topics.overview: Investigate causal and streaming model designs, frame and hop requirements, lookahead, state handling, computational efficiency, and deployment constraints relevant to sub-10 ms operation. Distinguish algorithmic, buffering, inference, I/O, and measured end-to-end system latency, recording absent values as "not reported."

sub_topics.title: NeuroChain Novelty, Validation, and Paper Direction
sub_topics.overview: Evaluate the proposed closed-form formant-safety projection against the closest retrieved methods, then formulate and rank 5–8 feasible technical contributions. Select one three-month direction and specify datasets and licensing, baselines, ablations, objective and listening evaluations, latency tests, statistical analysis, IEEE-style paper structure, comparison tables, and fully traceable references.

content: Literature Foundation for Low-Latency Vocal Enhancement
